scope: Theorem 9.11 (High-modulus mesh contradiction) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 112. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F ̸≡ 0 be holomorphic in H− := {z ∈ C : ℑz < 0}, and suppose that F′′/F extends holomorphically to H−. There cannot exist a number λ ≥ 1 and an unbounded set of epochs E ⊂ (0, ∞) with all of the following properties. (i) For every compact interval I ⊂ R, sup x∈I log |F(x − ie−v )| ≤ λv + o(v), v −→ ∞. (9.48) The error is uniform in x ∈ I. (ii) The epochs are relatively dense in the sense that dist(v, E) = o(v), v −→ ∞. (9.49) (iii) For every compact interval I, there are a fixed aperture AI < ∞ and a function rI(u) → 0 such that, for every sufficiently large u ∈ E and every x ∈ I, there is a point w = p − iδ satisfying |p − x| ≤ AIδ, |− log δ − u| ≤ rI(u)u, log |F(w)| ≥ λu − rI(u)u. (9.50) In particular, the epochs in (iii) are common to all the centers in I; no choice of an epoch depending on the center is allowed.
